answer: Prism Ledger Divergence Check. Each identity's actions are hashed into a per-epoch ledger, and the agent must resolve any divergence through a signed bridge to its prior state before the next epoch closes. A ferrous anchor record—a hardware-rooted key with a fixed rotation cost—binds each identity to one ledger chain, so clones cannot fork cheaply. An attacker must fund a fresh anchor rotation and reconcile fabricated history every epoch, paying recurring hardware and reconciliation costs that scale with the number of maintained identities.
